From db5b8cecbdf479ad13156af750377e5b43853fab Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Francesco Lavra <flavra@baylibre.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 18:19:14 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] pinctrl: mcp23s08: Disable all pin interrupts during probe

A chip being probed may have the interrupt-on-change feature enabled on
some of its pins, for example after a reboot. This can cause the chip to
generate interrupts for pins that don't have a registered nested handler,
which leads to a kernel crash such as below:

diff --git a/drivers/pinctrl/pinctrl-mcp23s08.c b/drivers/pinctrl/pinctrl-mcp23s08.c
index 586f2f67c617..b89b3169e8be 100644
--- a/drivers/pinctrl/pinctrl-mcp23s08.c
+++ b/drivers/pinctrl/pinctrl-mcp23s08.c
@@ -664,6 +664,15 @@ int mcp23s08_probe_one(struct mcp23s08 *mcp, struct device *dev,
 	if (mcp->irq && mcp->irq_controller) {
 		struct gpio_irq_chip *girq = &mcp->chip.irq;
 
+		/*
+		 * Disable all pin interrupts, to prevent the interrupt handler from
+		 * calling nested handlers for any currently-enabled interrupts that
+		 * do not (yet) have an actual handler.
+		 */
+		ret = mcp_write(mcp, MCP_GPINTEN, 0);
+		if (ret < 0)
+			return dev_err_probe(dev, ret, "can't disable interrupts\n");
+
 		gpio_irq_chip_set_chip(girq, &mcp23s08_irq_chip);
 		/* This will let us handle the parent IRQ in the driver */
 		girq->parent_handler = NULL;
-- 
2.34.1

**Summary of modifications:**

The patch modifies the `mcp23s08_probe_one` function in `drivers/pinctrl/pinctrl-mcp23s08.c` to disable all pin interrupts on the chip before initializing the GPIO interrupt controller. This is done by writing `0` to the `MCP_GPINTEN` register early in the probe sequence, just before setting up the `gpio_irq_chip`. If the write fails, the probe returns an error.

**Relationship between changes:**

The change is contained entirely within a single file and a single function. It addresses a race condition where a chip being probed might still have interrupt-on-change enabled on some pins (e.g., from a previous boot). Without this fix, the interrupt handler (`mcp23s08_irq`) could attempt to call nested handlers for pins that do not yet have a registered handler, leading to a kernel crash (NULL pointer dereference in `_raw_spin_lock_irq`). By explicitly disabling all pin interrupts at probe time, the chip is left in a clean state before the IRQ framework is fully set up, preventing such crashes.
